facility.name: Busy Bee Learning Center
facility.programs_provided: School Age Care,Before School Care,Meals Provided ,After School Care,Snacks Provided,Drop-In Care,Part Time Care,Transportation to/from School

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records -Training Hours: Certificates for health/safety trainings were not available for review for two out of four staff records reviewed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records -Training Hours (26 TAC §746.901(6))

occurrences.finding: Children's Products- Review list and Remove unsafe products: The US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) recall list has not been reviewed. .
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Products- Review list and Remove unsafe products (26 TAC §746.4135(a))

occurrences.finding: Written Activity Plan - Group Name and Dates: The activity plan posted in the toddler room was not current. The date on the activity plan were 8/26 -30/2024.      Note: This was CORRECTED during the inspection when a current activity plan was posted.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Activity Plan - Group Name and Dates (26 TAC §746.2205(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Written Operational Policies - Preventing and Responding to Abuse and Neglect: The operational policies reviewed were missing the following information:    Preventing and responding to abuse and neglect of children, including:     (A) Required annual training for employees;     (B) Methods for increasing employee and parent awareness of issues regarding child abuse and neglect, including warning signs that a child may be a victim of abuse or neglect and factors indicating a child is at risk for abuse or neglect;     (C) Methods for increasing employee and parent awareness of prevention techniques for child abuse and neglect;     (D) Strategies for coordination between the center and appropriate community organizations; and     (E) Actions that the parent of a child who is a victim of abuse or neglect should take to obtain assistance and intervention, including procedures for reporting child abuse or neglect;
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Operational Policies - Preventing and Responding to Abuse and Neglect (26 TAC §746.501(a)(26))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing Before Eating: Six school age children did not have their hands washed before eating their snack, after arriving to operation.    NOTE: This was addressed with the caregiver during the inspection and children were directed to wash their hands.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing Before Eating (26 TAC §746.3417(1))

occurrences.finding: Director Annual Training 30 Hours Required: The director was missing annual training on the following topics:     (1)  Recognizing and preventing shaken baby syndrome and abusive head trauma;    (2)  Understanding and using safe sleep practices and preventing sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS);     (3)  Understanding early childhood brain development.    (4)  Preventing and controlling the spread of communicable diseases, including immunizations;    (5)  Administering medication, if applicable, including compliance with 746.3803 of this chapter (relating to What authorization must I obtain before administering a medication to a child in my care?); and    (6)  Preventing and responding to emergencies due to food or an allergic reaction;
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Annual Training 30 Hours Required (26 TAC §746.1311(a))

occurrences.finding: CPR Training and Recertification Adhere to Guidelines-skill based: Two caregivers obtained their CPR training online.
occurrences.violation_type_title: CPR Training and Recertification Adhere to Guidelines-skill based (26 TAC §746.1315(b)(1))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required: A caregiver was missing annual training for training year 3/26/2022-3/25/2023 on the following topics:    (1)  Recognizing and preventing shaken baby syndrome and abusive head trauma;    (2)  Understanding and using safe sleep practices and preventing sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS); and    (3)  Administering medication, if applicable, including compliance with 746.3803 of this chapter (relating to What authorization must I obtain before administering a medication to a child in my care?).
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required (26 TAC §746.1309(a))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: Several electrical outlets were observed in the pre-k room without a safety cover. One electrical outlet was observed in the toddler room without a safety cover.     Television cords were observed hanging connected to an extension cord. This posed a safety hazard as the electrical outlets and television cords were within children's reach.     Note: This was CORRECTED during the inspection as safety covers were placed on the electrical outlets and the television cords were removed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Chairs - Safety Straps Used if Required by Manufacturer: An infant observed sitting at a kidney shaped table  did not have the safety straps fastened.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Chairs - Safety Straps Used if Required by Manufacturer (26 TAC §746.4501(b))

occurrences.finding: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean: A hole was observed on a wall in the afterschool room. The hole measured 3 1/2 inches wide and 3 inches high and was accessible to children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: Emergency Evacuation and Relocation Diagram - Posted in Each Room: An emergency evacuation and relocation diagram was not posted in the toddler room.        Note: This was CORRECTED during the inspection as the diagram was posted near the entrance of the room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Emergency Evacuation and Relocation Diagram - Posted in Each Room (26 TAC §746.5207(b))

occurrences.finding: Infant May Not Sleep in a Restrictive Device: An infant was observed sleeping on a floor bouncer for an undetermined amount of time.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant May Not Sleep in a Restrictive Device (26 TAC §746.2426)

occurrences.finding: Children's Records Maintained: A child's admission form was missing the following information:     A statement of the child s special care needs. This includes, but is not limited to, allergies, existing illness, previous serious illness and injuries, hospitalizations during the past 12 months, and any medications prescribed for continuous, long-term use; and     A  signed statement from the parent giving the name and address of a health-care professional who has examined the child within the past year stating that the child is able to participate in the program.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records Maintained (26 TAC §746.603(a))

occurrences.finding: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Not Set Up During Other Activities: A pre-k child was observed napping on a floor mat in the carpet area  during other activities.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Not Set Up During Other Activities (26 TAC §746.2909(2))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees and Caregivers - Pre-service Training: Two caregivers did not complete 24 clock hours of  pre-service training in the specific required topics. A caregiver with a DOE 4/4/2022 was missing 4 clock hours of training and a caregiver with DOE 3/02/2022 was missing 7 clock hours of training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees and Caregivers - Pre-service Training (26 TAC §746.1301(2)(A))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records: 3 of 5 personnel records reviewed were missing a notarized Licensing Affidavit for Applicants for Employment form. 2 of 5 personnel records reviewed were missing a statement signed and dated by the employee showing he has received a copy of the child-care center s: Operational policies; and Personnel policies.  A statement signed and dated by the employee verifying the date the employee  attended training during orientation. The director had an expired driver's license.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records (26 TAC §746.901)

occurrences.finding: Children's Records Maintained: 2 of 6 children's files reviewed were missing the child's current immunization record. 3 of 6 children's records reviewed were missing the address, and telephone number of the child s physician or an emergency-care facility. A child's record reviewed was missing the parent's authorization to obtain emergency medical care and to transport the child for emergency medical treatment. A child's record reviewed was missing the name and telephone number of the school that a school-age child attends. A child's record reviewed was missing the Vision and hearing screening results.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records Maintained (26 TAC §746.603(a))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: Several children's disposable face masks and a used band-aid were observed in the outdoor play ground accessible to children.        Note: This was CORRECTED during the inspection as the face masks and  used band-aid  were disposed of.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Active Play Surfacing In Use Zones - Loose Fill or Unitary Surfacing: A slide that required surfacing was observed in the children's outdoor playground.           Note: This was CORRECTED during the inspection as the slide was removed from the playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Active Play Surfacing In Use Zones - Loose Fill or Unitary Surfacing (26 TAC §746.4901(a))

occurrences.finding: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually: Three caregivers that conduct transportation did not have current training in transportation safety.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually (26 TAC §746.1316(a))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required: A caregiver with DOE 5/30/2018 was missing 12 clock hours of annual training.     A caregiver with DOE 3/26/2021 was missing annual training on the following topics:     Emergency preparedness;     Preventing and responding to emergencies due to food or an allergic reaction; and     Handling, storing, and disposing of hazardous materials including compliance with 746.3425 of this chapter (relating to Must caregivers wear gloves when handling blood or bodily fluids containing blood?).
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training Area - 24 Hours Required (26 TAC §746.1309(a))

occurrences.finding: First Aid Kit - Incomplete Kit: The first aid kit in the transportation vehicle was incomplete. The following items were missing:    1.Adhesive tape;  2. cotton balls; and    3.thermometer        Note: This was CORRECTED during the inspection as the missing items were obtained and included in the first aid kit.
occurrences.violation_type_title: First Aid Kit - Incomplete Kit (26 TAC §746.4003(a))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Documentation that Crib Meets Applicable Federal Rules: There was no documentation available for review to verify that a crib in the infant room met applicable federal rules at Title 16, Code of Federal Regulations, Parts 1219or 1220, concerning  Safety Standards for Full Size Baby Crib".
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Documentation that Crib Meets Applicable Federal Rules (26 TAC §746.2409(a)(9))

occurrences.finding: Policies Comply with Rules: The operational policies reviewed were incomplete. The following information was missing:    The Promotion of indoor and outdoor physical activity that is consistent with Subchapter F of this chapter (relating to Developmental Activities and Activity   Plan); your policies must include:    (A) The benefits of physical activity and outdoor play;    (B) The duration of physical activity at your operation, both indoor and outdoor;    (C) The type of physical activity (structured and unstructured) that children may engage in at your operation;    (D) Each setting in which your physical activity program will take place;    (E) The recommended clothing and footwear that will allow a child to participate freely and safely in physical activities; and    (F) A plan to ensure physical activity occurs on days when extreme weather conditions prohibit or limit outdoor play.    The procedures for parents to participate in the child-care center s operation and activities.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Policies Comply with Rules (26 TAC §746.201(1))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: A pack of plastic edging stakes were observed on the ground in the outdoor playground. This posed a safety hazard as the plastic stakes were accessible to children. The artificial grass rug on the outdoor playground was not secured and presented a tripping hazard for children when playing outdoors.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Food Service and Preparation Requirement - Safe and Sanitary: Expired milk was served to children during the lunch meal. Several milk gallons stored in the refrigerator had an expiration date of 4/11/2022.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Service and Preparation Requirement - Safe and Sanitary (26 TAC §746.3317)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Children in Control: A caregiver did not ensure that children in the after school room were not out of control. Children were observed running around the running and sitting under tables. No activities were provided by the caregiver.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Interact positively with children (26 TAC §746.1203(5))

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Fire Extinguisher: The fire extinguisher in the transportation vehicle was located in the trunk and not secured in the passenger compartment and accessible to the caregiver.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Fire Extinguisher (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(5))

occurrences.finding: Infant Daily Report - Share with Parent: Infant daily reports were not being completed or shared with parents on a daily basis. The last daily report available for review was dated 4/8/2022.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Daily Report - Share with Parent (26 TAC §746.2431)

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Employees' Attendance: Time sheets were not maintained for a caregiver present at the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Employees' Attendance (26 TAC §746.801(5))

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Emergency Medical Information: The  Emergency medical transport and treatment authorization forms, and Parent s names and telephone numbers and emergency telephone numbers were not available in the transportation binder for two children being transported.      Note: This was CORRECTED during the inspection as the required forms were obtained and included in the transportation binder.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - Emergency Medical Information (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Written Activity Plan - Outdoor Play Opportunities: Children were not being provided with outdoor play twice a day. According to the center director the children did not go out to the outdoor playground this morning due to it being too windy outside.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Activity Plan - Outdoor Play Opportunities (26 TAC §746.2206(1))
